title: Federated checkers affirm entries they never measured; a dropped 'v' silences the whole chain
summary: Both federated checkers print an affirmative success message naming entries they did not check. check-federated-pins.mjs reports market.plugins.length ('3 plugin(s) checked') when it only ever checks v-prefixed tag pins - opum-output-styles tracks main and is always skipped. check-federated-content.mjs reports the KEYS OF THE BASELINES FILE as 'verified', not what it resolved, so it names opum-lore and opum-quest as verified even on a run that resolved neither. Consequence: a pin bump that drops the leading v (v0.7.0 -> 0.7.0) makes checkEntry return null in BOTH checkers, zero network calls happen, and CI stays fully green while printing 'federated pins OK (3 plugin(s) checked)' and 'federated content OK (2 pinned entry/entries verified: opum-lore, opum-quest)'. The manifest shape step accepts it (it requires s.ref to exist, not to be version-shaped) and lore-check accepts it (version=${ref#v} leaves 0.7.0 intact). The entire federation verification chain becomes a silent no-op on a one-character typo, and says so affirmatively.
description:
Raised as a hypothesis by the lore-cli session on 2026-09-15 (routed via opum-agent) after its own post-publish read-back gate was found to have three defects a fully green run could not see. lore-cli named opum-marketplace as likely to share the shape and said plainly it had not looked.

The structural half of its hypothesis does NOT apply here: both federated assertions are already extracted into scripts/ with real suites (5/5 and 8/8 passing, run locally at 432b959). What the suites do not reach is the 'if (import.meta.url === ...)' CLI main block, which is where the success message is composed. So the assertion is tested and the CLAIM about the assertion is not - lore-cli's third question ('what does the success message claim versus what it measured') lands even though its first two do not.

Measured, not inferred. Copied both scripts and the baselines to a scratch dir, rewrote marketplace.json with the leading v stripped from both tag pins, and ran them unmodified:
  refs now: opum-lore=0.7.0, opum-output-styles=main, opum-quest=0.7.1
  federated pins OK (3 plugin(s) checked)                                          exit=0
  federated content OK (2 pinned entry/entries verified: opum-lore, opum-quest)    exit=0
Ran ci.yml's inline manifest node block against the same file: 'manifests OK (3 plugin(s): ...)' exit 0. Ran lore-check's inline ref resolution: 'Declared lore version: 0.7.0 (from opum-lore ref 0.7.0)' - would pass.

Note the second message is the worse of the two: it is not merely over-counting, it names specific entries as verified on a run where neither was fetched, because 'checked' is derived from Object.keys(baselines) rather than from what checkMarketplace actually resolved.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each checker reports only what it actually resolved: the count and names come from the entries checkEntry did not skip, not from market.plugins.length or from the baselines file keys
A run that skips an entry says so by name and why (branch pin, sha pin, not a v-tag), so a skipped entry is visible rather than absorbed into an OK count
A pin whose ref is version-shaped but missing the leading v is caught rather than silently skipped - either the manifest shape step rejects it, or the checkers treat it as in-scope

Tests cover the CLI main block's reporting, not only checkEntry/checkMarketplace: a suite asserts the exact success message for a mixed index (one v-pin, one branch pin) and for an index where every pin is out of scope
Both halves proven separately and the versions recorded: the new tests red on the dropped-v fixture above, green on a clean tree, with every other job green on both SHAs

implementationNotes: The dropped-v scenario is the cheapest reproduction but not the only one. Any future entry added without a baseline is already caught by check-federated-content (tested: "a v-pin with no baseline at all fails"), so the gap is specifically entries that fall out of scope at the /^v/ test.

check-federated-content.mjs is the better model for the fix on counting, but it is currently wrong in a different way than check-federated-pins.mjs: pins over-counts (reports all plugins), content mis-attributes (reports baseline keys as verified). Fixing one by copying the other would carry the second defect across.

Do not widen the /^v/ scope without thinking about opum-output-styles, which pins ref main deliberately - it has no fixed content by design and must stay out of scope. The ask is that its exclusion be STATED, not that it be checked.

TEST-AUTHORING TRAP, from lore-cli 2026-09-15 after implementing the same fix shape on its own gate. An assertion over a gate's REPORTING has to distinguish the instruction from the explanation of the instruction - a distinction the assertion side never has to make. lore-cli asserted its checklist contained no 'grep' and the test failed, because the checklist legitimately QUOTES the old grep to explain why it went. The naive assertion would have pushed the next author to delete the reasoning to get the test green. Scope any such test to the machine-readable part (the count, the named list, the emitted command block), never to the prose around it - our success strings sit next to long explanatory comments and the same trap applies.

lore-cli found the same market.plugins.length shape in its own gate (success line printed REGION_IDS.length while the comparison loop carries a continue) and reports an honest asymmetry worth preserving here: theirs was never observed to lie, because a prior clause fails any missing region before the line is reached - a guard, not an identity. OURS WAS OBSERVED TO LIE: 3 claimed, 2 checked, today, with no fixture needed. Do not soften this task's framing to match theirs.

TWO-HALVES PROOF, run ids recorded because exit codes alone do not say what was measured. GREEN HALF: e144ff6, run 35023251971, job 104563973632 - check - manifests, Tracker integrity and lore check all success, and the log shows all 8 report cases executing rather than the step being skipped. RED HALF: 72953d0, run 35023378280, throwaway PR #111 closed unmerged - a deliberately false assertion injected into report.test.mjs. check - manifests FAILED at the step 'Checker reports say what was actually measured' with 'FAIL pins: mixed index miscounted', and the other 7 cases still passed, while lore check and Tracker integrity stayed GREEN on that same SHA. So the job moved for its own reason rather than because something general broke, and the failure is the one expected rather than a different red wearing the same colour.

Why the red half was worth a throwaway PR rather than inferring it from the local mutation run: the mutation check proved the SUITE'S LOGIC goes red. That a non-zero exit from that step actually reddens the CI check is WIRING, a separate object, and nothing had measured it - opum-web (OWEB-8) raised exactly this distinction hours earlier about its own guard-proof job. Versions: node 24.20.0 local and CI, quest 0.7.1.
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #110, squashed to dev at 04b8794; required checks green on e144ff6 (check - manifests, Tracker integrity, lore check) and the new step confirmed present in the run log rather than inferred from the green - job 104563973632 in run 35023251971 shows all 8 report cases executing.

Both checkers now derive their summary from what actually ran. Scope has one source of truth, classifyEntry, exported from the pin checker and imported by the content checker, so the two cannot drift on what 'in scope' means. checkMarketplace returns { problems, checked/verified, skipped }; out-of-scope entries print by name and reason; a run that checks nothing says NOTHING WAS CHECKED instead of OK; an unreferenced baseline is noted rather than counted; and a version-shaped ref with no leading v is a named failure instead of a silent skip, which closes the reported trap.

scripts/test/report.test.mjs covers the CLI main block the other two suites cannot reach - it runs each checker as a subprocess against fixture working directories and asserts the emitted text, not the exit code. Wired into ci.yml unconditionally.

21/21 across three suites. Mutation-checked SELECTIVELY per lore-web's technique: restoring market.plugins.length reddens only the pins count case, restoring the baseline-keys list only the content case, and making the dropped v a silent skip again reddens both dropped-v cases and nothing else - a uniformly red run would have meant the suite tests identity rather than properties. Live run: 'federated pins OK (2 of 3 entries checked: opum-lore, opum-quest; 1 out of scope, listed above)', where it previously claimed 3 of 3.

Two incidental findings during the work, both instances of the defect this task is about. The report suite first passed 0/8 with EMPTY OUTPUT because macOS tmpdir() returns /var/... while import.meta.url resolves /private/var/..., so the scripts' import.meta.url === argv[1] guard was false and the CLI block never ran - a suite that exercises nothing and reports a clean exit. Fixed with realpathSync and the reason recorded in the test. Then it deadlocked: execFileSync blocks the event loop that has to answer the child's fetch to the in-process fixture server. Now async.

Versions: node 24.20.0 locally and in CI, quest 0.7.1, gh authenticated. OMARK-58 remains To Do at High.
